excluded_seen: The first look (look.py, exploratory): the pair on side 1024 and soup 19 on side 512, from starts 7001 to 7016, read through blocks of 4 to 32. Every number predicted here comes from it, and its late rule is the one tried in X.
The instrument's tests: the pair and soups on sides 32 to 128 from starts 9001 on.
The earlier studies of this world (starts 101 to 228, 2001 to 2032, 3001 to 3032, 4001 to 4016, 5001 to 5016, 6001 to 6384), none of them read through blocks.
Nothing has been read through blocks on side 2048, or through blocks of 64 on any side, and no start from 8001 on has been generated or run.
body.source: docs/scale-up-plan.md, step 4; the first look in examples/scale-up-closure
body.statement: Life against HighLife under the standoff is read through blocks with the clock at the block, and a supercell records whether its block moved. On a torus twice as wide as the first look's, from fresh starts and at blocks up to twice as large: stillness is stable (S); the neighbours sharpen the odds without changing the best guess (N); the rule with neighbour counts is the same rule early and late, and the rule without them is not (T); the rule learned on the smaller torus serves on the larger (X); one of its chances is the same at every block (E); and run on by itself it keeps up with the fine world for eight coarse generations and then loses it (H).
body.title: Does a coarse rule for movement stand in for the fine world?
